questions.questionText: Your company wants administrators to securely SSH into Compute Engine virtual machines that do not have external public IP addresses. You want to avoid setting up a traditional VPN or managing a bastion host. Which Google Cloud service should you use?
options: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for TCP forwarding
Cloud NAT
Serverless VPC Access
Google Cloud Armor
correctAnswers: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for TCP forwarding

explanation.general explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for TCP forwarding allows you to establish a secure, encrypted tunnel over the internet to access SSH (port 22) and RDP (port 3389) on your private VM instances, authenticating the user via Google Identity without needing a bastion host or VPN.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT allows outbound internet access for private VMs; it does not allow inbound SSH or RDP connections.
why other options are wrong.Serverless VPC Access: This is used to connect serverless environments (like Cloud Run) to a VPC, not for administrative SSH access.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud Armor: Cloud Armor protects web applications from DDoS and HTTP-based attacks, not SSH traffic.

questions.questionText: You are deploying an internal corporate web application on Google Cloud. You want employees to access it from anywhere on the internet securely, without requiring a client VPN. You want access to be strictly based on their Google Workspace identity. What should you use?
options: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Cloud VPN
VPC Service Controls
Cloud Router
correctAnswers: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)

explanation.general explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) implements Zero Trust access by verifying a user's identity (via Google Workspace or Cloud Identity) before granting them access to web applications, eliminating the need for a traditional corporate VPN.

why other options are wrong.Cloud VPN: Cloud VPN requires setting up an IPsec network connection, which acts as a traditional network perimeter rather than an identity-based zero-trust proxy.
why other options are wrong.VPC Service Controls: VPC SC mitigates data exfiltration from Google APIs; it does not act as an identity-based proxy for custom web applications.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Router: Cloud Router is used for dynamic BGP routing with VPNs and Interconnects, not for web application access control.

questions.questionText: Historically, managing SSH keys for dozens of developers across hundreds of virtual machines has been an operational nightmare. Which Google Cloud feature centralizes SSH access control by linking it directly to IAM roles, eliminating manual SSH key management?
options: OS Login
Cloud KMS
Secret Manager
Identity Platform
correctAnswers: OS Login

explanation.general explanation: OS Login links your Linux user account to your Google identity (IAM). When you use OS Login, you don't need to manually manage SSH keys in the `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` files on the instances; access is granted or revoked instantly based on IAM roles.

why other options are wrong.Cloud KMS: Cloud KMS manages encryption keys for data at rest, not SSH access keys for VM administration.
why other options are wrong.Secret Manager: Secret Manager securely stores API keys and passwords, but it does not natively integrate with the Linux SSH daemon to manage user access.
why other options are wrong.Identity Platform: Identity Platform adds identity and access management functionality to your applications (like customer login), not OS-level SSH access.

questions.questionText: To further secure remote access via Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP), your security team wants to enforce policies where users can only access the application if their laptop has an up-to-date operating system and screen lock enabled. Which Google Cloud capability provides this?
options: Context-Aware Access
VPC Firewall Rules
Cloud Identity Groups
Binary Authorization
correctAnswers: Context-Aware Access

explanation.general explanation: Context-Aware Access (built upon BeyondCorp principles) allows you to define granular access policies based on the context of the request, such as device posture (OS version, screen lock status), user location, and IP address.

why other options are wrong.VPC Firewall Rules: Firewalls evaluate traffic based on IP addresses and ports at the network layer; they cannot evaluate device posture or OS health.
why other options are wrong.Cloud Identity Groups: Groups manage user identity collections but do not verify the security state of the device the user is connecting from.
why other options are wrong.Binary Authorization: Binary Authorization ensures only trusted container images are deployed on GKE; it has nothing to do with end-user device posture.

questions.questionText: Your private Compute Engine VMs (with no external IP addresses) need to securely back up data to a Cloud Storage bucket. To ensure this traffic never traverses the public internet, which networking feature must be enabled on the VPC subnet?
options: Private Google Access
Cloud NAT
Serverless VPC Access
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
correctAnswers: Private Google Access

explanation.general explanation: Private Google Access is a subnet-level setting that allows VM instances with only internal IP addresses to securely reach the external IP addresses of Google APIs and services (such as Cloud Storage) over Google's private internal network.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT provides outbound access to the general public internet, which is unnecessary since Google APIs can be reached internally.
why other options are wrong.Serverless VPC Access: This connects serverless environments (like Cloud Run) to a VPC, not a VPC to Google APIs.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP secures inbound user access to VMs and web apps, not outbound VM access to Google APIs.

questions.questionText: You are configuring Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for TCP forwarding to allow secure SSH access to your internal VMs. Which two configuration steps are strictly required for this to work?
options: Create a VPC firewall rule allowing ingress traffic from the `35.235.240.0/20` IP range.
Grant the user the `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor` IAM role.
Deploy an External Application Load Balancer in front of the VMs.
Assign external public IP addresses to all VMs.
Enable Cloud NAT on the VPC network.
correctAnswers: Create a VPC firewall rule allowing ingress traffic from the `35.235.240.0/20` IP range.
Grant the user the `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor` IAM role.

explanation.general explanation: To use IAP for TCP forwarding, you must allow traffic from Google's IAP proxy IP range (`35.235.240.0/20`) to reach your VMs via a firewall rule. You must also grant the user the `iap.tunnelResourceAccessor` IAM role, which gives them authorization to use the tunnel.

why other options are wrong.Deploy an External Application Load Bala: A load balancer is required for IAP HTTP/HTTPS access, but it is NOT required for IAP TCP forwarding (SSH/RDP).
why other options are wrong.Assign external public IP addresses to a: The primary benefit of IAP is that you do NOT need public IPs. Assigning them defeats the purpose.
Cloud NAT is for outbound internet access, which is not required for inbound IAP tunnels.

questions.questionText: In cloud network architecture, what is the primary purpose of a Bastion Host (also known as a Jump Server)?
options: To provide a single, heavily monitored, and secured entry point to access internal private networks from the internet.
To cache static web content and deliver it globally with low latency.
To automatically translate private IP addresses to public IP addresses for outbound internet traffic.
To dynamically balance HTTP traffic across multiple web server instances.
correctAnswers: To provide a single, heavily monitored, and secured entry point to access internal private networks from the internet.

explanation.general explanation: A Bastion Host is a specialized, highly secured computer on a network specifically designed and configured to withstand attacks. It serves as a single gateway (jump server) for administrators from the public internet to securely access private instances residing in internal subnets.

why other options are wrong.To cache static web content and deliver: This is the function of a Content Delivery Network (CDN).
why other options are wrong.To automatically translate private IP ad: This is the function of a NAT (Network Address Translation) Gateway.
why other options are wrong.To dynamically balance HTTP traffic acro: This is the function of a Load Balancer.

questions.questionText: You want to protect a custom-built, internal Human Resources web application using Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP). To enable IAP for HTTP/HTTPS web applications, the application MUST be deployed behind which Google Cloud component?
options: External or Internal Application Load Balancer
Cloud Router
Cloud NAT Gateway
Serverless VPC Access Connector
correctAnswers: External or Internal Application Load Balancer

explanation.general explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for web applications works by intercepting web requests at the load balancer level. Therefore, the web application must be a backend service behind an External or Internal Application Load Balancer (formerly HTTP/S Load Balancer).

why other options are wrong.Cloud Router: Cloud Router is for BGP routing in hybrid networks, not for load balancing or HTTP proxying.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT Gateway: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access, not inbound HTTP/HTTPS proxying.
why other options are wrong.Serverless VPC Access Connector: This is for connecting serverless apps to a VPC, not a requirement for IAP.

questions.questionText: Your team has deployed a Cloud Function that requires access to a legacy on-premises database. The on-premises network is connected to your VPC via Cloud VPN. How can you securely route traffic from the Cloud Function to the on-premises database?
options: Configure a Serverless VPC Access connector to bridge the Cloud Function to the VPC.
Assign a static public IP address to the Cloud Function and whitelist it on-premises.
Use Private Google Access on the Cloud Function.
Enable Cloud NAT on the Cloud VPN gateway.
correctAnswers: Configure a Serverless VPC Access connector to bridge the Cloud Function to the VPC.

explanation.general explanation: A Serverless VPC Access connector allows serverless environments (like Cloud Functions, Cloud Run, and App Engine) to send requests directly into a VPC network using internal IPs. Once the traffic is in the VPC, it can route over the Cloud VPN to the on-premises network.

why other options are wrong.Assign a static public IP address to the: Cloud Functions do not natively support assigning static public IPs for outbound traffic without going through a VPC and NAT, and this approach sends traffic over the public internet rather than the secure VPN.
why other options are wrong.Use Private Google Access on the Cloud F: Private Google Access is for VPC VMs to reach Google APIs, not for serverless functions to reach VPC/on-prem resources.
why other options are wrong.Enable Cloud NAT on the Cloud VPN gatewa: Cloud NAT translates private IPs to public IPs for internet access; it is not used for internal VPN routing.

questions.questionText: A modern Zero Trust security architecture (like Google's BeyondCorp) shifts access controls from the network perimeter to individual users and devices. Which two Google Cloud services are central to building a Zero Trust architecture for web applications?
options: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Context-Aware Access
Cloud NAT
Dedicated Interconnect
VPC Peering
correctAnswers: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Context-Aware Access

explanation.general explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) enforces identity-based access control, and Context-Aware Access evaluates the security posture of the user's device and context (IP, location, OS). Together, they form the foundation of Google's Zero Trust / BeyondCorp architecture.

why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT is a traditional network component for outbound internet access, unrelated to Zero Trust application access.
why other options are wrong.Dedicated Interconnect: This provides a physical private connection to GCP, which is a traditional perimeter-based networking solution.
why other options are wrong.VPC Peering: VPC Peering connects internal networks together, not a component for Zero Trust user access.

questions.questionText: You need to securely connect an on-premises data center to a Google Cloud VPC over the public internet. The connection must support automated dynamic routing. Which service should you choose?
options: HA VPN
Dedicated Interconnect
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Partner Interconnect
correctAnswers: HA VPN

explanation.general explanation: HA (High Availability) VPN securely connects your on-premises network to your VPC network through an IPsec VPN connection over the public internet. It requires Cloud Router to provide dynamic routing (BGP).

why other options are wrong.Dedicated Interconnect: Dedicated Interconnect provides a private, dedicated physical connection; it does not traverse the public internet.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP is for user-level access to applications and VMs, not for network-to-network (site-to-site) connectivity.
why other options are wrong.Partner Interconnect: Partner Interconnect uses a service provider to create a private connection, bypassing the public internet.

questions.questionText: When implementing Context-Aware Access policies for remote workers, you want to require that the connecting device is company-owned and has disk encryption enabled. Which Chrome Enterprise component collects and provides this device posture information to Google Cloud?
options: Endpoint Verification
Chrome Remote Desktop
Google Cloud Armor
OS Login
correctAnswers: Endpoint Verification

explanation.general explanation: Endpoint Verification is a Chrome extension and native OS agent that gathers device posture information (such as OS version, disk encryption status, and screen lock) and reports it to Google Cloud, allowing Context-Aware Access policies to make access decisions based on device health.

why other options are wrong.Chrome Remote Desktop: This is a tool for remote controlling a computer, not for reporting device security posture.
why other options are wrong.Google Cloud Armor: Cloud Armor protects against web threats and DDoS; it does not query local device hardware states.
why other options are wrong.OS Login: OS Login manages SSH keys via IAM; it does not monitor end-user device health.

questions.questionText: Your remote developers need to connect to a private Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL database from their local laptops. The database only has a private internal IP address. What is the most secure and managed way to provide this access without deploying a VPN?
options: Run the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy locally and tunnel it through an IAP-enabled Bastion host.
Temporarily assign a public IP address to the Cloud SQL instance and whitelist their home IP.
Configure Cloud NAT to route traffic directly to the developers' laptops.
Use Serverless VPC Access directly from the developers' laptops.
correctAnswers: Run the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy locally and tunnel it through an IAP-enabled Bastion host.

explanation.general explanation: To securely access a private-IP-only Cloud SQL instance from outside the VPC without a VPN, developers can SSH into a Bastion host using IAP TCP forwarding, and use the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy to securely tunnel the database connection through that Bastion host.

why other options are wrong.Temporarily assign a public IP address t: Assigning a public IP violates the security requirement of keeping the database strictly private, and developer home IPs change frequently.
why other options are wrong.Configure Cloud NAT to route traffic dir: Cloud NAT is for outbound internet access from the VPC; it cannot route inbound traffic to the database.
why other options are wrong.Use Serverless VPC Access directly from: Serverless VPC Access is strictly for Google Cloud serverless resources (like Cloud Run); it cannot be installed on developer laptops.

questions.questionText: Your organization uses Windows virtual machines on Compute Engine. Administrators need to use Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) to manage these servers. The servers do not have public IP addresses. How can you facilitate secure RDP access over the internet?
options: Use IAP for TCP forwarding to tunnel the RDP connection (port 3389).
Use OS Login to manage Windows credentials.
Deploy an External Application Load Balancer and terminate RDP.
Use Cloud Armor to whitelist the RDP port.
correctAnswers: Use IAP for TCP forwarding to tunnel the RDP connection (port 3389).

explanation.general explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for TCP forwarding supports any TCP port. By tunneling port 3389 through IAP, administrators can use their standard RDP clients to connect securely to Windows VMs that only have internal IP addresses.

why other options are wrong.Use OS Login to manage Windows credentia: OS Login is specifically designed for Linux environments (SSH); it does not support Windows RDP.
why other options are wrong.Deploy an External Application Load Bala: Application Load Balancers only support HTTP, HTTPS, and HTTP/2; they do not proxy raw RDP (TCP port 3389) traffic.
why other options are wrong.Use Cloud Armor to whitelist the RDP por: Cloud Armor is a WAF that attaches to HTTP(S) load balancers. It does not provide remote desktop access.

questions.questionText: Your on-premises servers need to securely upload files to a Google Cloud Storage bucket. You have a Dedicated Interconnect in place. How can you ensure the traffic goes over the Interconnect rather than the public internet?
options: Configure Private Google Access for on-premises hosts.
Enable Cloud NAT on the VPC.
Set up VPC Service Controls.
Use a Global External Application Load Balancer.
correctAnswers: Configure Private Google Access for on-premises hosts.

explanation.general explanation: Private Google Access for on-premises hosts allows on-premises systems to reach Google APIs and services (like Cloud Storage) over an existing Cloud Interconnect or Cloud VPN connection, keeping the traffic entirely off the public internet.

Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access for GCP VMs; it does not route on-premises traffic to Google APIs.
VPC Service Controls protect against data exfiltration; they do not inherently provide the routing path for on-premises hosts to reach APIs.
why other options are wrong.Use a Global External Application Load B: Load balancers expose services to the internet. This would bypass the private Interconnect entirely.

questions.questionText: When implementing OS Login for a fleet of Linux virtual machines in Google Cloud, which two security benefits do you gain over traditional SSH key management?
options: Access is automatically revoked when a user is removed from Cloud IAM.
It eliminates the need to manually manage `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` files on the VMs.
It automatically blocks SSH traffic from unauthorized countries.
It encrypts the VM's Persistent Disk automatically.
It provides a built-in GUI for remote desktop access to Linux.
correctAnswers: Access is automatically revoked when a user is removed from Cloud IAM.
It eliminates the need to manually manage `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` files on the VMs.

explanation.general explanation: OS Login links SSH access directly to Google Cloud IAM. Because of this, if a user's IAM permissions are revoked, their SSH access is instantly terminated. Furthermore, it completely replaces the manual, error-prone process of copying public SSH keys into local `authorized_keys` files on the VM.

why other options are wrong.It automatically blocks SSH traffic from: Blocking traffic by geography requires network-level controls (like firewalls or Cloud Armor), not OS Login.
why other options are wrong.It encrypts the VM's Persistent Disk aut: Persistent Disks are encrypted by default, but this has nothing to do with OS Login.
why other options are wrong.It provides a built-in GUI for remote de: OS Login manages CLI SSH access; it does not provide a GUI remote desktop environment.

questions.questionText: You want to enforce the use of OS Login across all existing and future Compute Engine instances within a specific Google Cloud project. What is the most efficient way to enable this globally for the project?
options: Set the metadata key `enable-oslogin=TRUE` in the project-level metadata.
Run a startup script on every VM to install the OS Login agent.
Create a VPC firewall rule to block all standard SSH port 22 traffic.
Change the IAM roles of all users to 'OS Login Admin'.
correctAnswers: Set the metadata key `enable-oslogin=TRUE` in the project-level metadata.

explanation.general explanation: You can enable OS Login across an entire project by setting the custom metadata key `enable-oslogin` to `TRUE` at the project level. All VMs in the project inherit this metadata and will automatically start enforcing OS Login.

why other options are wrong.Run a startup script on every VM to inst: Google Cloud images already have the guest environment installed; you just need to flip the metadata switch to enable it.
why other options are wrong.Create a VPC firewall rule to block all: OS Login still uses SSH on port 22. Blocking the port would lock everyone out.
why other options are wrong.Change the IAM roles of all users to 'OS: While users need the OS Login IAM role, applying the metadata flag is what actually tells the VMs to use the feature.

questions.questionText: Which specific IAM role must be granted to a user so they can utilize Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) to establish a TCP forwarding tunnel (e.g., for SSH) to a Compute Engine VM?
options: roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor
roles/compute.networkAdmin
roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor
roles/compute.osLogin
correctAnswers: roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor

explanation.general explanation: The `roles/iap.tunnelResourceAccessor` role grants the specific permission needed to route TCP traffic through the IAP tunnel to access resources like VMs. Without this role, the user's connection will be rejected by the IAP proxy.

why other options are wrong.roles/compute.networkAdmin: This role manages VPC networks and firewalls, but does not grant authorization to use the IAP tunnel.
why other options are wrong.roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor: This role is used to grant access to web applications behind IAP (HTTP/S), not for TCP forwarding.
why other options are wrong.roles/compute.osLogin: This grants permission to log into the VM OS, but does not grant the network-level permission to pass through the IAP tunnel.

questions.questionText: Your company wants to establish secure, dedicated remote access connectivity from your physical data center to your Google Cloud VPC environment. Which two Google Cloud services are designed to provide this hybrid network connectivity?
options: Cloud VPN
Cloud Interconnect
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Serverless VPC Access
Cloud NAT
correctAnswers: Cloud VPN
Cloud Interconnect

explanation.general explanation: Cloud VPN and Cloud Interconnect are the primary Google Cloud services used to establish secure, high-bandwidth hybrid connectivity between external on-premises networks and Google Cloud VPCs.

why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP provides application-level and VM-level access for end-users over the internet, not site-to-site network connectivity.
why other options are wrong.Serverless VPC Access: This connects GCP serverless resources (Cloud Run) to a VPC, not on-premises data centers.
why other options are wrong.Cloud NAT: Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access for private VMs; it does not connect data centers.

questions.questionText: When deciding between Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) and a traditional corporate VPN for remote employee access to web applications, what is a primary security advantage of IAP?
options: IAP provides per-resource access control, whereas a VPN typically grants broad access to the entire network.
IAP requires the installation of a heavy client application on every user's device.
IAP encrypts data at rest automatically, while VPNs only encrypt data in transit.
IAP bypasses all Google Cloud IAM policies for faster access.
correctAnswers: IAP provides per-resource access control, whereas a VPN typically grants broad access to the entire network.

explanation.general explanation: Traditional VPNs operate at the network layer; once authenticated, a user often has broad lateral access to the internal network. IAP operates at the application layer (Zero Trust), verifying identity and context for every single request to a specific resource, offering much finer-grained security.

why other options are wrong.IAP requires the installation of a heavy: IAP for web apps requires only a standard web browser, making it much lighter than VPN clients.
why other options are wrong.IAP encrypts data at rest automatically,: IAP manages access control and transit encryption, it has nothing to do with data at rest.
why other options are wrong.IAP bypasses all Google Cloud IAM polici: IAP heavily relies on IAM policies to determine who gets access; it does not bypass them.

questions.questionText: Which security philosophy assumes that the network perimeter is inherently insecure and that every request to access a system must be authenticated, authorized, and continuously validated before granting access?
options: Zero Trust
Defense in Depth
Castle-and-Moat
Network Address Translation
correctAnswers: Zero Trust

explanation.general explanation: Zero Trust (the foundation of Google's BeyondCorp architecture) shifts access controls from the network perimeter to individual users and devices. It assumes no network is safe, requiring strict identity and context verification for every single request.

why other options are wrong.Defense in Depth: Defense in depth uses multiple overlapping layers of security, but doesn't specifically mandate the 'never trust, always verify' model for every request.
why other options are wrong.Castle-and-Moat: This is the traditional perimeter security model that Zero Trust aims to replace.
why other options are wrong.Network Address Translation: NAT is a networking routing technique, not a security philosophy.

questions.questionText: A developer working from a coffee shop needs to temporarily run `kubectl` commands against a private Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. The cluster control plane only has a private IP address. What is the most secure way for the developer to access the cluster?
options: Set up an IAP TCP forwarding tunnel to a Bastion host in the VPC, and route `kubectl` traffic through it.
Add the coffee shop's public IP address to the GKE cluster's Authorized Networks list.
Assign a public IP address to the GKE control plane temporarily.
Use a Serverless VPC Access connector from the developer's laptop.
correctAnswers: Set up an IAP TCP forwarding tunnel to a Bastion host in the VPC, and route `kubectl` traffic through it.

explanation.general explanation: A highly secure pattern for accessing private GKE clusters from unmanaged or remote networks is to deploy a tiny Bastion host VM inside the VPC. The developer uses IAP to securely SSH into the Bastion (or tunnels traffic through it) and then communicates with the private GKE control plane from within the VPC.

why other options are wrong.Add the coffee shop's public IP address: This requires the cluster to have a public endpoint enabled, which violates the requirement for a strictly private control plane.
why other options are wrong.Assign a public IP address to the GKE co: This exposes the control plane to the internet and degrades the cluster's security posture.
why other options are wrong.Use a Serverless VPC Access connector fr: Serverless VPC Access connectors cannot be used from local laptops; they are only for GCP serverless resources.

questions.questionText: You are developing a Cloud Function that needs to process sensitive data and store it in an internal-only Cloud SQL database. How do you configure the network so the Cloud Function can securely access the internal VPC resources?
options: Deploy a Serverless VPC Access connector in the same region and configure the function to use it.
Enable Cloud NAT on the default VPC network.
Configure the Cloud Function to use a static external IP address.
Assign the `roles/compute.networkUser` IAM role to the Cloud Function.
correctAnswers: Deploy a Serverless VPC Access connector in the same region and configure the function to use it.

explanation.general explanation: Serverless VPC Access allows serverless environments, such as Cloud Functions, to connect directly to a VPC network using internal IP addresses. This is required to securely access internal resources like a private Cloud SQL instance.

why other options are wrong.Enable Cloud NAT on the default VPC netw: Cloud NAT is used to give VMs outbound internet access, not to route serverless traffic into a VPC.
why other options are wrong.Configure the Cloud Function to use a st: This sends traffic over the public internet, which cannot reach a private internal database.
why other options are wrong.Assign the `roles/compute.networkUser` I: IAM roles handle permissions, but the physical network path bridging serverless to VPC requires the VPC Access connector.

questions.questionText: To prevent developers from creating a security vulnerability, your security team wants to ensure that no Compute Engine instances can ever be assigned a public, external IP address across the entire organization. Which two methods can enforce or facilitate this rule?
options: Implement the `compute.vmExternalIpAccess` Organization Policy constraint.
Configure Private Google Access on all subnets.
Create a VPC firewall rule to block port 80 and 443.
Remove the 'Compute Instance Admin' role from all developers.
Use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) to encrypt all traffic.
correctAnswers: Implement the `compute.vmExternalIpAccess` Organization Policy constraint.
Configure Private Google Access on all subnets.

explanation.general explanation: The most direct way to categorically block external IPs is using the Organization Policy constraint `compute.vmExternalIpAccess`. However, because VMs without public IPs still need to reach Google services (like Cloud Storage), you must also configure Private Google Access on the subnets to facilitate this internal architecture.

why other options are wrong.Create a VPC firewall rule to block port: Blocking ports does not prevent a developer from assigning a public IP to a VM.
why other options are wrong.Remove the 'Compute Instance Admin' role: This stops developers from doing their jobs entirely, rather than just enforcing a secure network boundary.
why other options are wrong.Use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) to encryp: While IAP provides secure remote access to internal VMs, it is not the mechanism that prevents the assignment of public IPs.

questions.questionText: Which underlying protocol does Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) use to encapsulate and tunnel SSH and RDP traffic from the public internet into your VPC network?
options: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol)
IPsec (Internet Protocol Security)
correctAnswers: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)

explanation.general explanation: IAP encapsulates traffic using TCP. The feature is literally called 'IAP TCP forwarding'. It establishes a WebSocket/HTTPS connection over TCP to Google's edge, which then unpacks the raw TCP traffic (like SSH on port 22 or RDP on port 3389) and forwards it to the VM.

why other options are wrong.UDP (User Datagram Protocol): IAP currently does not support forwarding UDP traffic.
why other options are wrong.ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol): IAP does not forward ICMP traffic (you cannot use standard `ping` through an IAP tunnel).
why other options are wrong.IPsec (Internet Protocol Security): IPsec is used by Cloud VPN, not by IAP.

questions.questionText: Referencing the Mountkirk Games case study: Mountkirk requires secure administrative access to their global fleet of backend game server VMs. To reduce the attack surface, these VMs only have internal IP addresses. What is the Google-recommended approach to grant admins remote CLI access to these servers?
options: Use IAP TCP forwarding to tunnel SSH connections to the game servers.
Deploy an External passthrough Network Load Balancer and map port 22 to all servers.
Configure Cloud NAT to allow inbound SSH connections from administrator IPs.
Assign ephemeral public IP addresses to the game servers during maintenance windows.
correctAnswers: Use IAP TCP forwarding to tunnel SSH connections to the game servers.

explanation.general explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) TCP forwarding is the standard, most secure method for providing administrative SSH access to internal-only VMs. It relies on IAM authentication and requires no public IPs or exposed ports on the VMs.

why other options are wrong.Deploy an External passthrough Network L: This exposes SSH directly to the internet, which is a massive security risk and violates the 'internal IP only' requirement.
why other options are wrong.Configure Cloud NAT to allow inbound SSH: Cloud NAT is strictly for outbound traffic and does not support inbound connections.
why other options are wrong.Assign ephemeral public IP addresses to: This is operationally cumbersome and temporarily breaks the security posture by exposing the servers.

questions.questionText: Referencing the EHR Healthcare case study: They need to securely transmit sensitive on-premises patient data to Google Cloud storage systems without traversing the public internet. Which hybrid connectivity solution best meets their strict compliance and high-bandwidth requirements?
options: Dedicated Interconnect
HA VPN
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP)
Serverless VPC Access
correctAnswers: Dedicated Interconnect

explanation.general explanation: Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct, physical, high-bandwidth (10 Gbps or 100 Gbps) connection between an on-premises network and Google's network. Because it bypasses the public internet entirely, it perfectly satisfies strict healthcare compliance and privacy requirements.

why other options are wrong.HA VPN: While secure (IPsec), HA VPN traffic travels over the public internet, which violates the strict requirement to avoid public internet traversal.
why other options are wrong.Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP): IAP provides application-level user access, not site-to-site data transmission connectivity.
why other options are wrong.Serverless VPC Access: This is for connecting serverless GCP apps to a VPC, not for on-premises to cloud connectivity.

questions.questionText: You are managing access to a global internal web application. Can Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) provide access control for users distributed globally, and if so, how is it deployed?
options: Yes, because IAP is applied to the Global External Application Load Balancer.
Yes, but you must deploy a separate IAP instance in every region.
No, IAP only supports regional deployments for internal users.
No, IAP only works with Cloud VPNs which are region-specific.
correctAnswers: Yes, because IAP is applied to the Global External Application Load Balancer.

questions.questionText: You are designing a highly secure network architecture using a Bastion Host. Which two configurations are considered mandatory best practices for securing the Bastion Host itself?
options: Only allow inbound SSH access via IAP TCP forwarding (or strictly whitelisted corporate IP ranges).

It must be heavily secured by restricting inbound access (ideally using IAP so no public IP is needed at all) and placing it in an isolated network segment with strict egress firewalls to prevent lateral movement if compromised.
